answer.rationale: Assembly line at 94% utilization with no buffer, plus 14-day expiry, makes supplier continuity fragile. memory_c1 supports avoiding migration risk (no interruption, stable integration through cycles). memory_c6 shows that extending term length on incumbent relationship unlocks volume pricing without narrowing service. memory_c4 confirms renewal renegotiation recovers real margin. The contract does not auto-renew, so doing nothing (defer) risks a lapse. Switching primary vendor (memory_c2) cut cost sharply last year but reintroduces migration risk under tight timeline and high utilization. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses supply resilience but cannot fix the 18% spend cut within 14 days and would require onboarding time. Negotiating terms with the incumbent keeps integration and deliveries stable, fits the 14-day window, and combines memory_c1's continuity with memory_c6's volume-pricing insight and memory_c4's margin recovery evidence. This is the lowest-risk path to TCO reduction given the operational state.
